findings.title: Unusable appliedId read as no gateway
findings.problem: readDesktopGatewayState returns namesGateway: false when _meta.json has an appliedId that is not a string or fails isSafeSessionId, the same answer as an absent appliedId. A config that names an entry the reader refuses to open is unreadable, not a disconnect.
findings.impact: Narrow trigger: Desktop would have to write a non-string or unsafe appliedId. In that case a not-connected daemon follows its tracked sessions while another gateway may be collecting them, against the spec's 'unreadable config is not followed'. No effect for well-formed Desktop configs.
findings.recommendation: When meta.appliedId is present but rejected by appliedConfigId, return namesGateway: true (e.g. `namesGateway: isRecord(meta) && meta.appliedId !== undefined`), and add a gateway test row for it.

findings.title: First by-id pass fires on the remembering poll
findings.problem: startByIdIfDue returns early while nothing is remembered without moving lastPassAt. When the interval has elapsed since the last pass, the first id finalizeInactive remembers gets a by-id pass on the same poll, so a just-failed END is re-sent within milliseconds rather than at the 10-minute interval.
findings.impact: Trigger: the first failed finalization while not connected after a quiet stretch of 10+ minutes. Cost: one extra real delivery attempt that counts toward MIN_REAL_ATTEMPTS in delivery-budget.ts. Budget exhaustion still needs the retry window to elapse, so no record is dropped.
findings.recommendation: Have the remembering path start the interval (for example, set lastPassAt when remember() adds to an empty memory), or accept the immediate retry and note it in the interval docs.

disposition.rationale: Accepted as is: one extra real attempt on the remembering poll after a quiet stretch; the delivery budget needs the retry window to pass, so no record is dropped.

findings.title: Re-remembered-during-pass branch untested
findings.problem: The guard `if (this.undeliveredIds.get(sessionId) !== order) continue;` that keeps an id re-remembered while a by-id pass is in flight is not exercised by any test: every by-id test remembers before the pass starts and awaits it.
findings.impact: Trigger: a pass whose sends outlast a poll interval while a session finalizes in the same window. If the guard regressed, a re-remembered undelivered id would be deleted or rotated to the back, delaying its END until the next connected listing pass. No current defect.
findings.recommendation: Add one runtime test that holds redeliverById open, remembers the same id during the pass, settles it, and asserts the id is still remembered and first in the next redeliverById batch.

disposition.rationale: Accepted as is: the branch is not reachable today, a remembered record is already finalised and untracked; the guard stays as correct by construction.

findings.title: Stop's final poll can start an unawaited by-id pass
findings.problem: stop() sets stopped and runs a final poll. On the not-connected branch, redelivery.startByIdIfDue(now) has no stopped guard, so that poll can start a detached by-id pass that stop() never awaits. The connected branch's listing pass already behaves the same way at base.
findings.impact: Trigger: stop while not connected, with remembered ids and the interval elapsed. If stopDaemon's SIGKILL cuts the pass mid-send, the record stays completed and is delivered again by the next start. That re-delivery path already exists and the ticket scopes out an unfinished stop, so the worst case is a repeated send attempt, not lost data.
findings.recommendation: Guard with `if (!this.stopped) this.redelivery.startByIdIfDue(now);`, or await redelivery.pass in stop() before the finalization loop.
